lines.japanese: ブックストア。ファミリーレストラン。レンタルビデオショップ。ガソリンスタンド。
lines.english: Bookstore. Family restaurant. Video store. Gas station.

lines.japanese: 夜を徹して輝きつづけるロードサイドのサイン看板が、色とりどりの帯となってガラスの向こうへ流れてゆく。
lines.english: Roadside signs blazing through the night streamed past the glass in bands of color.

lines.japanese: 目を転じてダッシュボードの時計を見た。俺のうたた寝はほんの十分足らずだったみたいだ。
lines.english: I glanced at the dashboard clock. I couldn’t have been asleep for even ten minutes.

lines.japanese: 「あら、起こしちゃった？」
lines.english: “Oh, did I wake you?”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いや、悪りぃ」
lines.english: “Uh, no. Sorry.”

lines.japanese: 「いまの発進、急だったかね」
lines.english: “Did I pull out too suddenly?”

lines.japanese: 「いやいや、ぜんぜん。も、ちょお滑らかだった」
lines.english: “No, no, not at all. It was, like, incredibly smooth.”

lines.japanese: 適当なことを言いながら、寝返りをうつみたいに座りなおした。
lines.english: I gave her a vague answer and shifted in my seat as if I were rolling over in bed.

lines.japanese: それからしばらく俺たちは、窓に飛びこんでくる景色に他愛もない難癖をつけたりして、断続的な会話を楽しんだ。
lines.english: For a while, we traded idle complaints about the scenery passing our windows, our conversation coming and going.

lines.japanese: 信号に引っかかって止まったとき、照明を落として暗く静かに眠っているケータイショップが目に入った。
lines.english: When a red light stopped us, I noticed a cell-phone shop sleeping dark and silent, its lights turned down.

lines.japanese: 「あ、そうだ」
lines.english: “Oh, right.”

lines.japanese: 俺はふと、パルさんに聞くことがあったのを思いだした。
lines.english: I suddenly remembered something I had meant to ask Paru.
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: パルさんがこっちを見ながら、くわえた煙草に火を点ける。モーターの音が鳴って、運転席側の窓が細く開いた。
lines.english: Paru looked my way as she lit the cigarette between her lips. A motor whirred, and the driver's window opened a crack.

lines.japanese: 「ああ、いや──」
lines.english: “Uh, no—”

lines.japanese: 信号が青に変わった。オートマ車の運転手は、片手に煙草を挟んだままアクセルを踏んだ。白い煙は吸いこまれるように窓の外へ流れていった。
lines.english: The light turned green. Paru stepped on the gas, still holding her cigarette in one hand. White smoke streamed out the window as if drawn away.

lines.japanese: 「あんさ。パルさん、ポケベルの使い方って分かる？」
lines.english: “Hey. Paru, you know how to use a pager?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　なに、いきなり」
lines.english: “Huh? Where'd that come from?”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、ちょっと。で、どうなの。分かんのポケベル」
lines.english: “Oh, it’s just a little thing. So? You know how to use one?”
“Seven-five-four-two-nine-five-zero-three.”

lines.japanese: いきなり八つの数字を一息に唱えて、やつは窓枠に肘を載せたまま得意げに煙草を吸いこんだ。
lines.english: She rattled off all eight digits in a single breath, then took a smug drag from her cigarette with her elbow still perched on the window frame.
“...Huh? What was that?”

lines.japanese: 「もちろん、って言ったんだよ」
lines.english: “I said, ‘Of course.’”

lines.japanese: 「え、いまのが？」
lines.english: “What, that's what those numbers mean?”

lines.japanese: 「自慢じゃないけど、あたしゃいまだにケータイだって、ポケベル入力の出来る機種しか使わないからね。あるイミ現役だよ」
lines.english: Not to brag, but even now I only use cell phones that let me type pager-style. So in a way, I'm still an active pager user.

lines.japanese: 「うそ、すげえ。じゃあちょっと教えてくんない」
lines.english: “No way. That's amazing. Then could you teach me?”

lines.japanese: パルさんは勿体つけるように煙草を一息吸って、吐いた。
lines.english: Paru took a long, suspenseful drag from her cigarette, then let out the smoke.

lines.japanese: 「いいけどなんだい、いまどき」
lines.english: “Sure, but why now, of all times?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、だから、まあちょっとだよ。まあちょっとポケベル持ってるやついて、まあちょっとメッセージとか送ってみようかと思って。まあちょっと」
lines.english: “Like I said, it's just this little thing. I just happen to know somebody with a pager, and I just thought maybe I'd send a little message. Just a little.”
“Who?”

lines.japanese: 「だから、まあちょっと」
lines.english: “Like I said. Just somebody.”

lines.japanese: 「ふうん」
lines.english: “Hmm.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあコンビニ寄ったら、公衆電話使って教えてやるよ」
lines.english: “When we stop at the convenience store, I'll show you on the pay phone.”

lines.japanese: 「マジで。あーさんきゅ、助かるわ」
lines.english: “Seriously? Ah, thanks. That helps.”

lines.japanese: これであいつに「母親からの心あたたまるメッセージ」を送れる。めでたしめでたしの予感がして、俺は大きく息を吐いた。
lines.english: Now I could send her “a heartwarming message from her mother.” I let out a long breath. This was starting to look like a happy ending.

lines.japanese: 「ところで、ぜんぜん関係ない話なんだけどさ」
lines.english: “By the way, this is completely unrelated...”

lines.japanese: 「ん、なに」
lines.english: “Hm? What?”

lines.japanese: パルさんがハンドルを大きく切って、左に９０度曲がりながら言った。俺はヘッドレストにもたせた頭を運転席側へ曲げた。
lines.english: Paru spoke as she swung the wheel hard and made a ninety-degree turn to the left. Head still against the headrest, I turned toward the driver's seat.

lines.japanese: 「鳴って、いまだにポケベル使ってるらしいよ」
lines.english: “Apparently Naru still uses a pager.”

lines.japanese: 「知ってた？」
lines.english: “You knew that?”

lines.japanese: やつはわざわざ煙草を灰皿に預け、にたりと笑った。俺はでっかい舌打ちをした。
lines.english: She went so far as to park her cigarette in the ashtray before giving me a broad, knowing grin. I clicked my tongue, loudly.

lines.japanese: しかもパルさんがそのあと何も言葉を継がないものだから、車内は居心地の悪い沈黙に包まれてしまった。
lines.english: Worse, Paru said nothing else, and an awkward silence settled over the car.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、俺もぜんぜん関係ない話なんだけどさ」
lines.english: “Well, I've got something completely unrelated too.”

lines.japanese: 仕方ないので俺から口を開いた。
lines.english: No one else was saying anything, so I started.

lines.japanese: 「あの、なんつーか、俺いま惚れてる女いんだけど──」
lines.english: “See, there's this girl I'm in love with right now, and—”

lines.japanese: 「──うおっ！　ちょっ、危ねえなおまえ、前見ろ前」
lines.english: “—Whoa! Hey, watch it! Eyes on the road!”

lines.japanese: 「あ、ああ、悪い……ついびっくりして……」
lines.english: “Ah—yeah, sorry... You caught me by surprise...”

lines.japanese: 「で、あんさ、告白とかってどういう風にしたらいいの」
lines.english: “So, uh, how are you supposed to tell somebody you love them?”

lines.japanese: 「ほー、そうさねえ……」
lines.english: “Oh-ho. Let's see...”

lines.japanese: 運転手は口を横に広げてにたにた笑いながら、煙草を灰皿の上でねじり潰した。
lines.english: The driver stretched her mouth into a wide grin and stubbed out her cigarette in the ashtray.

lines.japanese: 「まー、そりゃおまえ、する側のキャラとかされる側の好みがあるからねえ。一概に正解ってのはないんじゃないかい」
lines.english: Well, that depends on the kinda person doing the confessing and what the person on the other end likes, doesn't it? No one right answer, I'd say.

lines.japanese: 「あー、そりゃそうだろうけどさ。でも、一般的にはこうじゃね？みたいの、そーゆーのないの」
lines.english: “Yeah, sure, but isn't there some normal way people do it? Something like that?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、私だったら『君のクレープを一生食べつづけたい』とか言われたいねェ」
lines.english: “Hmm. Me, I'd like somebody to say, ‘I want to eat your crêpes for the rest of my life.’”

lines.japanese: 「なんだそりゃ。ぜんぜん一般的じゃねーじゃん」
lines.english: “What the hell is that? That’s not normal at all.”

lines.japanese: 「うるっさいなあ、なんだよ一般的って。夜景を見ながら『君の瞳に乾杯』みたいのか？」
lines.english: “Oh, shut up. What does normal even mean? Watching the city lights while you tell her, ‘Here's looking at you, kid’?”

lines.japanese: 「えええ、そんなん都市伝説だろ。マジでそんなん言うやついんの」
lines.english: “What? That's an urban legend. Does anybody actually say crap like that?”

lines.japanese: 「だろ？　カッコつけたらそうなっちゃうんだから、告白なんてなァ自然でいいんだよ自然で」
lines.english: “Exactly. Try to act suave and that's where you end up. A confession ought to be natural. Natural.”

lines.japanese: 「カッコつけが似合うやつならそれもいいけどさ、そうじゃないんだったらそんな気張るこたないって」
lines.english: “If you can pull off suave, fine. If you can’t, don’t force it.”

lines.japanese: 「ほー。そんなもんか」
lines.english: “Huh. That how it works?”

lines.japanese: 「そうだよ。流れに任せて、な？　自然と言いたくなったときに、その言いたくなったことをそのまま言やあ、まあ、それでいいんじゃないかねえ」
lines.english: “That's how it works. Go with the flow, okay? When the words come naturally, just say whatever it is you naturally want to say. That should do.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。つまりなに、アドリブでいいってこと」
lines.english: “Right. So I can improvise.”

lines.japanese: 「そーそー。そんなさ、前もって用意したしゃらくさいセリフ棒読みするよりもさ、おまえらしい飾らない言葉をぶつけた方が相手も喜ぶってなもんさ」
lines.english: “Exactly. Forget reading off some corny line you prepared ahead of time. Just hit her with your own honest words, and she’ll like that a lot better.”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん。そーゆーもんかね」
lines.english: “Hmm. You really think so?”

lines.japanese: 「そーゆーもんさ。気持ちさえ伝わりゃあ、べつにちょっとぐらいカッコ悪くたっていいんだよ。なんたって、そういう不器用さもあんたの魅力のひとつなんだからさ」
lines.english: “That's how it works. As long as your feelings reach her, who cares if you look a little uncool? That clumsiness is part of your charm, after all.”

lines.japanese: 「……マジで」
lines.english: “...Seriously?”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょ、パルさんいいこと言うじゃん。俺、感動したよ。なんかいい風吹いてきた、朝日見えてきた」
lines.english: “Hey, Paru, that was actually good. I’m moved. I’ve got the wind at my back. I can see the sun coming up.”

lines.japanese: 「気合入ったか？」
lines.english: “Feeling fired up?”

lines.japanese: 「おー、はんぱねーよ。マジはんぱねーよ」
lines.english: “Hell yeah. I’m fired up like you wouldn’t believe.”

lines.japanese: 俺がこぶしを打つと、パルさんはふんと笑ってほんの少しだけオーディオのボリュームを下げた。
lines.english: I punched one fist into the other. Paru snorted and turned down the stereo just a fraction.

lines.japanese: 「ところで、またぜんぜん関係ない話なんだけどさ」
lines.english: “By the way, here's another completely unrelated subject...”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　なに」
lines.english: “Huh? What?”

lines.japanese: 「鳴はああ見えて、すっげえ臆病な子だからさ」
lines.english: “Naru may not look it, but she gets scared really easily.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ……ああ、まあ、そうな」
lines.english: “Yeah... Yeah, I guess she is.”

lines.japanese: 「泣かすような真似したらてめえのドタマかち割るよ」
lines.english: “You make her cry, I'll crack your skull open.”

lines.japanese: 「上等だっつーの」
lines.english: “Bring it on.”

lines.japanese: 俺は狭いシートの上で片あぐらを組んだ。
lines.english: I tucked one leg under me on the narrow seat.

lines.japanese: 車道沿いにコンビニエンスストアの白い直方体が迫ってきて、パルさんは左ウインカーを点滅させた。
lines.english: The white rectangular block of a convenience store drew near beside the road, and Paru switched on the left blinker.

lines.japanese: 「ゼロ、ニィ、ゼロ、の……」
lines.english: “Zero, two, zero, then...”

lines.japanese: 鳳からもらったメモを電話台の端に置いて、そこに並んでいた十桁の数字を打ちこむ。
lines.english: I set the note Ohtori had given me on the edge of the telephone shelf and entered the ten-digit number written on it.

lines.japanese: しばらくの無音状態。間。緊張しながら待っているうちに、受話器の向こうから機械的な女の声が聞こえてきた。
lines.english: Silence. A beat. Then, as I waited on edge, a mechanical woman’s voice came through the receiver.

lines.japanese: 「うおっ、繋がった繋がった」
lines.english: “Whoa, it connected! It connected!”

lines.japanese: 「そりゃ繋がるだろ」
lines.english: “Of course it connected.”

lines.japanese: 愛想いいんだか悪いんだか分からないトーンで女は言う。メッセージヲ入力シテクダサイ。
lines.english: In a tone I couldn't decide was friendly or hostile, the woman said: PLEASE ENTER YOUR MESSAGE.

lines.japanese: 「う、うおっ、やべえパルさん。なんかやる気のない女がメッセージ入れろっつってる」
lines.english: “Wh-whoa, Paru. Some woman who sounds bored out of her mind is telling me to enter a message.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ入れなよ、さっき教えた通り。はい、最初に＊２＊２」
lines.english: “Then enter it, just like I showed you. First, star-two-star-two.”

lines.japanese: 「お、おお。コメってこれか、この肛門か」
lines.english: “O-okay. This is the star? This little asshole?”

lines.japanese: 「アスタリスクな。あとはほら、これ見て頑張んな」
lines.english: “It's called an asterisk. Now look at this and do your best.”

lines.japanese: パルさんが別の紙を鳳メモの上に重ねる。さっき即席で作ってくれたポケベル打ち入力表だ。
lines.english: Paru laid another sheet over Ohtori's note: the pager-input chart she'd thrown together for me a moment ago.

lines.japanese: プッシュホン１２個のボタンの組み合わせで、１００以上の文字を生みだす魔法のレシピ。パルさんらが学生だった時代には、ほとんどの同級生がコレをすべて頭の中に入れていたらしい。なにもんだ、おまえら。
lines.english: A magic recipe for conjuring more than a hundred characters from combinations of the twelve buttons on a touch-tone phone. Apparently almost everyone in Paru's generation had the whole thing memorized back when they were students. What the hell were you people?

lines.japanese: 「あたしが打ってやった方が早いんだけどねえ」
lines.english: “It'd be faster if I entered it for you.”

lines.japanese: 「うるせえな、いいんだよ、んなのプライバシーの侵害じゃねえか。てめ、あっち向いてろ」
lines.english: “Shut up. That’d be an invasion of privacy. Turn around, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「いいけどあんた、もうメッセージは考えてあんだろうね」
lines.english: “Fine, but you’ve already figured out what you’re going to say, right?”

lines.japanese: 「おう、まあな。最初だからちょっと短めだけど」
lines.english: “Yeah, more or less. It's a little short, since it's the first one.”

lines.japanese: “元気でがんばれ　母より”
lines.english: Keep well, and do your best. —Mother

lines.japanese: それだけだ。
lines.english: That was all.

lines.japanese: それだけだけど、あいつは充分喜ぶんじゃないか……と思う。
lines.english: It wasn’t much, but I thought it might make her happy enough.

lines.japanese: 俺は人差し指を立てながら対応表に目を落とした。
lines.english: I poised my index finger and looked down at the conversion chart.

lines.japanese: 「えーっと、どこだ……げ、げ、げ……」
lines.english: “Let's see, where is it... Ge, ge, ge...”
“Two-four-zero-four.”

lines.japanese: 「おお、さんきゅ。２、４、０、４、っと」
lines.english: “Oh, thanks. Two, four, zero, four...”

lines.japanese: 「んで次がァ……ん、ん、ん……」
lines.english: “And next is... N, n, n...”
“Zero-three.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそっか、悪りぃ──」
lines.english: “Oh, right. Sorry—”

lines.japanese: 「──って、なんだよおまえ、いちいち聞いてんじゃねえよ。盗聴かコノヤロウ。てめ訴えんぞコラ、有線電気通信法違反とかで」
lines.english: —What the hell, why're you listening to every damn thing?! You wiretapping bastard. I'll sue your ass, y'hear? For violating the Wire Telecommunications Act or some crap!

lines.japanese: 「おまえがいちいち声に出すからだろ。黙って打ちなさいよ、黙って」
lines.english: “You're the one saying every little thing out loud. Enter it silently. Silently.”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、も、ぜってー言わねえ。ぜってー言わねえかんな」
lines.english: “Shut up. I'm never saying another word. Not one damn word.”

lines.japanese: 俺は気を取りなおして電話に向かった。
lines.english: I collected myself and faced the phone again.

lines.japanese: 「えーっと、そんで……２の２っと……」
lines.english: “Okay, then... two-two...”
“Ki.”
“Four-four, zero-four...”
“De.”
“Two-one, zero-four...”
“Ga.”

lines.japanese: 「なに、どうした。手ぇ止まってんじゃない」
lines.english: “What? What's wrong? You stopped typing.”

lines.japanese: 「……あのさ。あのさ、おばちゃん。な。いちいち解読してんじゃねえよ。盗聴かコノヤロウ。てめソレ、出るとこ出んぞ。法廷沙汰も辞さねえぞコノヤロウ」
lines.english: ...Listen. Listen, lady, okay? Stop decoding every damn thing. You wiretapping bastard. I'll see you in court for that. I ain't afraid to make a whole court case of it, asshole!

lines.japanese: 「だから、おまえがいちいち声に出すからだって。黙って打ちなさいよ、黙って」
lines.english: “I told you, you're saying every little thing out loud. Enter it silently. Silently.”

lines.japanese: 「っせえな、声出さねえと落ちつかねンだよ」
lines.english: “Shut up. I can't settle down unless I say it aloud.”

lines.japanese: 「しょーがないねえ。じゃあ終わるまで私、中で週刊誌でも読んでくるから──」
lines.english: “Honestly. Then I'll go inside and read a weekly magazine until you're finished—”

lines.japanese: 「え、ちょちょちょ、待て待て待て。待ってって。いや、いろよ、行くなよ。いきなりひとりじゃ何かと不安になっちゃうじゃねーか、てめ、初心者なめんなコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “Whoa, hey, hey—wait, wait, wait. Stay here. Don't go. You can't just leave a beginner alone with this; I'm nervous enough already. Don't underestimate me, asshole.”

lines.japanese: 「初心者のくせに態度でかいんだよ、指導者なめんなコノヤロウ」
lines.english: “You've got a big mouth for a beginner. Don't underestimate your instructor, asshole.”

lines.japanese: ぶちぶち文句垂れる教官を尻目に、俺は入力した文字を頭の中にひとつずつ並べていった。ゲ、ン、キ、デ、ガ、ン、バ、レ──よし。
lines.english: With my instructor bitching away in the background, I lined up the characters I'd entered in my head, one by one. GE, N, KI, DE, GA, N, BA, RE. Good.

lines.japanese: あとは『母より』か。
lines.english: All that remained was “From Mother.”

lines.japanese: えーっと……ハ、ハ、ハ……。
lines.english: Let's see... Ha, ha, ha...

lines.japanese: いや、待てよ……あいつ、お嬢だからな。ママとかのがそれっぽいかな。『ママより』。んん？　どうだ？
lines.english: No, wait... She was a rich girl. Maybe “Mama” would sound more like her. “From Mama.” Hmm. Would it?

lines.japanese: 「パルさん」
lines.english: “Paru.”

lines.japanese: 「あー？」
lines.english: “Yeah?”

lines.japanese: 「あんさ。社長ん家の娘って、やっぱカーチャンのことカーチャンって呼ばないの」
lines.english: “Hey. A company president's daughter probably doesn't call her mother ‘Ma,’ right?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ？　知るかい、そんなこと。うちはもんじゃ屋だよ」
lines.english: “What? How should I know? My family runs a griddle joint.”

lines.japanese: 「知るかいじゃねーだろ。諦めんなよ、イマジネーション働かせろよ。じゃあ、そしたらおまえ、もんじゃ会社の社長ん家のカーチャンはなんて呼ばれてんだよ」
lines.english: “Don’t give me ‘how should I know.’ Don’t give up. Use your imagination. So what do they call Mom in the griddle-company president’s house?”

lines.japanese: 「さあ？　もんじゃ会社の社長夫人？」
lines.english: “Who knows? The griddle-company president’s wife?”

lines.japanese: 「『元気でがんばれ。もんじゃ会社の社長夫人より』……え、いやソレ長すぎだろ。つかべつに、もんじゃ会社のはいらなくね？」
lines.english: “‘Keep your spirits up and do your best. From the griddle-company president’s wife’... No, that’s way too long. And do we really need the griddle-company part?”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ社長夫人か？」
lines.english: “Then the company president’s wife?”

lines.japanese: 「『元気でがんばれ。社長夫人より』……いや、それもねーだろ。つか、わざわざ娘に社会的地位アピるとか、それどんだけだよ。どんだけ虚栄心あふるるカーチャンだよ」
lines.english: “‘Keep your spirits up and do your best. From the company president's wife’... No, that's wrong too. Who announces her social standing to her own daughter? What manner of vanity overfloweth from this mother?”

lines.japanese: 「知らないよ。そんな言うなら自分で考えな」
lines.english: “I don’t know. If you’re going to complain that much, think of it yourself.”

lines.japanese: 「っだよ、使えねーやつだな。おまえなんかもうアレだ、もんじゃで例えるなら、あのエビっぽいなんかパリパリしたアレだ、もう」
lines.english: “The hell? You’re useless. If you were something from a griddle joint, you’d be that crispy little thing that sort of looks like a shrimp. That’s you.”

lines.japanese: 「あん？　てめえコノヤロ、よそモンのド素人が桜エビなめてんじゃねえぞチキショーめ」
lines.english: “Huh? Listen here, you bastard! Don't you goddamn clueless outsider dare look down on sakura shrimp, shithead!”

lines.japanese: 俺はもんじゃ屋の娘に右の頬をぐにぐに引っぱられながらプッシュボタンに向きなおった。しょーがねえ、さっさと残りを打ちこもう。
lines.english: The griddle-joint owner’s daughter pulled my right cheek this way and that while I turned back to the buttons. Fine. I’d hurry up and enter the rest.

lines.japanese: ……あれ？
lines.english: ...Huh?

lines.japanese: あ、やべ……さっき俺、どっちにしたんだっけ。母だっけママだっけ。
lines.english: Oh, crap... Which had I settled on? Mother or Mama?

lines.japanese: 「……えーと」
「ああドラ、言いわすれたけど、あんまりもたもたしてると時間切れンなるよ」
lines.english: “Oh, Drac, forgot to tell you: take too long and it'll time out.”

lines.japanese: 「え、マジで。そんなんあるの。やっべ、じゃあもう、どっちでもいいや」
lines.english: “What, seriously? It does that? Shit. Fine, either one.”

lines.japanese: もし多少の間違いがあっても、あいつは頭がいいからきっと行間を読みとってくれるに違いない。俺は急いで残りの文字を打ちこんだ。
lines.english: Even if I made a few mistakes, she was smart. Surely she'd read between the lines. I hurriedly entered the remaining characters.

lines.japanese: 「おっし──え、で、パルさんコレ最後どーすんだっけ」
lines.english: “All right—wait, Paru, how do I finish this again?”
“Pound twice.”

lines.japanese: 「シャープって、ああ、この○×ゲームの陣地みたいのか」
lines.english: “Pound... Oh, this tic-tac-toe-looking thing?”

lines.japanese: 俺は右下にある＃のボタンを続けて押した。機械的な声で女が言う。メッセージヲオ預カリシマシタ。
lines.english: I pressed the pound key at the lower right twice in succession. The mechanical woman said: YOUR MESSAGE HAS BEEN ACCEPTED.

lines.japanese: ふう。俺は額の汗を拭う振りをした。
lines.english: Whew. I pretended to wipe sweat from my brow.

lines.japanese: 「いやマジこれ、もう、めでたしめでたしだな」
lines.english: “Seriously, that settles everything. Happy ending all around.”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう」
lines.english: “Uh-huh.”

lines.japanese: あとはただ盗まれたチャリが戻ってくればいいだけ。そうすればポケベルと共に、この気の利いた思いやりがやつの元へ届くって寸法だ。
lines.english: Now the stolen bike just had to come back. Then the pager, along with this smooth little act of consideration, would make its way to her. That was the plan.

lines.japanese: それから俺たちはコンビニに入って、カップ麺とちょっとした菓子類を買っていった。
lines.english: After that, we went into the convenience store and bought cup noodles and a few snacks.

lines.japanese: 「あれ……でもさ、よく考えたら、チャリが見つかんねえから苦労してんじゃね？」
lines.english: “Wait... But now that I think about it, isn't she having all this trouble because they can't find the bike?”

lines.japanese: 「ああそう」
lines.english: “Uh-huh.”
